model: Qwen3.8-27B GGUF Q4_K_M, production profile, K3, D24 greedy, 20 ms window
method: campaign-artifacts/c1-k-sweep/stage_timing_compare.py: one model load, two identical explicit-MTP K3 requests (suite prompt code_merge_intervals, max_tokens 24) through the product HTTP route; legacy leg on the default evidence (legacy singleton verifier), packed leg after injecting the one-request packed_c1_target evidence row with the legacy verifier replaced by a guard; per-request adapter stage totals read from the resident runner rows (8 cycles each; both legs engaged, acceptance 0.652)
finding: Cycle structure is identical (8 vs 8 cycles, 2.95 tokens/cycle, acceptance 0.78/0.80 on the economics runs); the entire packed-vs-legacy throughput gap is per-cycle wall cost (+44 ms/cycle). The packed route's accept stage totals 459.3 ms per request (of which target_readback D2H 453.2 ms, ~56.7 ms/cycle) where the legacy graph route reports 0.0 - acceptance decisions round-trip through the host instead of staying on device. The packed target also runs eager (execution routes 'eager' x8) where the legacy singleton runs graph-captured ('graph' x8); the eager target itself is faster per cycle (252.6 vs 385.6 ms) so the graph gap is not the target cost - the host accept round-trip is the dominant, and the proposal path adds +21.3 ms per request (23 batch calls vs 0).
optimization_targets: device-side acceptance for the packed one-row frontier (eliminate the ~56.7 ms/cycle target readback; the legacy route already accepts on device)
graph-capture the packed one-row target pass (legacy proves graph works for the same verify shapes)
proposal batch-call overhead (+21.3 ms per request, 23 calls)
